decision.msg: merge.mjs: chose `git add -A -- <paths>` (chunked by 200) on EVERY landing, committed or not, over `git apply --index`: the three-way writer already has the final bytes in the tree, and apply --index would redo the merge. Alternative named: apply --index. Root cause found: when someone else had staged files, threeWay() skipped the add and printed 'left uncommitted', so new files stayed untracked; a failed commit also did `reset HEAD` on the paths. Now a post-check on `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` for `??` among the landed paths fails with exit 5 naming them (a modified live .jsonl is the site's own append, not a miss).

LandingCheck.verify: the real hole was the .merge-landed.json shortcut (written BEFORE the commit, returns landed on head match without looking at files). It now still checks every file the branch ADDED against michael/dev's tree and reports new_missing / 'new file not on dev'. Alternative: drop the ledger shortcut entirely; kept it for deleted/changed files to stay cheap.
